**Review result: the code is accepted. One body edit is needed (`needs-rework`): the line `Process change: yes`.**

Read-only review, not built here (your fork's code does not run on our runners; AGENTS.md). Your local gate report is recorded, not verified.

The code passes my read:
- The scope is right. The stacked parent (#2819) merged on 2026-11-20, so only the top commit is new: 6 files, +207/-27. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms it against current main.
- The unification is exact. The old `insert_text` body and `text::v_insert_text` do the same work (same `TextOptions`, same `InsertText::new`, same `profile_view`, same summary text). The MCP path now passes `[text, options]` to the verb, so script and MCP cannot drift.
- `only_keys` makes the MCP tool stricter: an unknown option is now refused by name instead of ignored. That is a fine direction for a refusal law, and you wrote it in the skill row and the rejections list.
- The verb table, `cam.d.ts` and the `TextProfile` interface agree; the pinned test `the_bindings_file_is_the_verb_table` keeps them agreeing.
- The rejections you list are enforced where you say: ranges, glyphs and name collisions in `InsertText` (from #2819, unchanged here), argument shape in the verb.
- `Fixes #2891` is right: the skill row and the script verb are what #2891 owed.

The one item: your PR changes `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, which is a process file (AGENTS.md, "Process files"). A PR that changes a process file must carry the line `Process change: yes` in its body (AGENTS.md, "Process changes bump PROCESS_VERSION"). Do not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` - the merging session bumps it. Add the line to the body and say so in a comment: the head does not move, so no re-review is owed; the label then returns to `merge-ready` at this head.

This is a `feat`, so it merges at the next minor cut, not before.
Added 'Process change: yes' to the pull request description. The git commit head was not changed.

Hi @NeoTech, gentle follow-up on this: the requested \Process change: yes\ line is in place in the PR description with the commit head unchanged.

Whenever you have a moment, could you please clear the \
eeds-rework\ label back to \merge-ready\ for the upcoming minor cut? Thank you!

<!-- pr-reviewer: 02d438403dc1f2f1ae792e921fbe171841b4fbb1 -->
**Re-check of head `02d438403`: clean.** Thank you for your patience, and for the `Process change: yes` line.

- **The one item of the review of 2026-11-21 is done.** The body has the line `Process change: yes`, and the PR does not change `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`. The head is the head of that review.
- **A new read (read-only Opus agent, nothing built) found no blocker.** `cam.insertText` builds the options and calls the command `InsertText` that is on `main`; it goes through the history, so undo works. The MCP tool `insert_text` now calls the same verb. The text geometry is the stroke font of `main`; this PR does not depend on #3395. Bad input is refused by name: the argument shape, unknown option keys, a `position` that is not 2 finite numbers, the offset limit, a setup with no stock, a height or spacing out of range, a character with no glyph. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` is in the new code outside tests.
- **One change of behaviour, stated in the skill row:** MCP `insert_text` now refuses unknown option keys. Before, it ignored them.
- **Merge.** `git merge-tree` with main `5721b0fff` is clean. The skill row lands one time and does not touch the rows that `main` changed.

Notes, not necessary for the merge:
1. The short form `insertText(text, height, options?)` works and has a test, but `cam.d.ts` does not show it. If the two heights are given, the positional one wins with no message.
2. `script/mod.rs` was 494 lines before this PR and is 503 lines with it.

**Labels.** `needs-rework` is removed and `merge-ready` is set with this comment: the requested change is done. A trial merge on the current main runs first (`insert_text`, `scripting`, `mcp_doc_drift`, `mcp_dxf`, `mcp`, clippy). The merge follows a green trial. After the merge, the `PROCESS_VERSION` bump is the work of the merging session.

Route note: the merge route is the coordinator's. Another session of this account merged this PR (`4dba7019d`) one minute after the re-check comment, before the trial merge here ran. A tip check of `main` at `4dba7019d` runs here (`insert_text`, `scripting`, `mcp`, `mcp_doc_drift`, `mcp_dxf`, clippy), and the post-merge run of the merge commit is the check of the tip. This PR changes a process file, so a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump is due.
